results.title: Russian strikes kill seven in Ukraine as Kyiv hits three refineries
results.content: Russia's drone attack killed people in six Ukrainian regions and hit a Naftogaz gas production facility, a DTEK thermal power plant and power networks in several parts of the country. Ukrainian drones struck Russian refineries in Samara and Rostov regions and an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region.

results.title: Haftar visits Ankara as Erdoğan prepares first Libya trip in 15 years
results.content: Eastern Libya's commander, accompanied by his son Saddam, met Turkey's defence and foreign ministers and its intelligence chief, days after Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian warship Merkury at Benghazi's naval base.

results.content: Puerto Rico's Jennifer Barreto wins Miss Universe 2026 in San Juan, becoming the pageant's first married winner and mother since 2023.

results.content: The US Virtual Embassy in Iran said Tehran, Yemen's Houthis and other aligned groups may target US interests and citizens in the region, including companies and institutions. results.content: Several hundred people gathered outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg to protest against a controversial bill that could allow unlimited authorisations for certain pesticides.

results.content: Good morning. Leo Cendrowicz here with your Wednesday newsletter. Today, we’re looking at the Western Balkans’ long road to EU membership, a Danish dilemma for Europe’s Socialists – and, courtesy of the late Pope Francis, a few encounters with the devil himself.

results.content: Thousands of teachers marched in Santiago during a nationwide strike against proposed budget cuts to public and higher education, with some protesters clashing with police.

results.content: The crew will carry out more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests. according to China's state media reports.

results.content: Switzerland opened the office on 19 October, when Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis travelled to Pyongyang and met senior officials, including his counterpart Choe Son Hui.

results.content: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella arrived in Villavicencio at around 9 am local time on Tuesday as he prepared to hold a security meeting and visit the scene of the blast.

results.content: An investigation into alleged surveillance of Indonesia’s president has widened into a treason case against senior police figures. It has already led to dismissals and parliamentary scrutiny, with police alleging a plot to undermine Prabowo’s government.

results.title: Colombia: At least 25 injured in bombing as armed violence resurges
results.content: At least 25 people were injured in a bombing in Villavicencio, damaging government buildings, businesses and vehicles. Meanwhile, hundreds of residents marched with candles in Cúcuta following a separate attack, amid a resurgence of armed violence in Colombia.

results.title: Italy develops 'ambitious' business with 'strategic partner' Azerbaijan, Tajani tells Euronews
results.content: Italy's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Euronews that Rome has sought to expand its business relations with Baku now that peace has brought stability and improved connectivity to the region.

results.title: Migrant caravans head north through Mexico towards US border
results.content: Migrants from several Central American countries are travelling through southern Mexico in a caravan, hoping to reach the United States.

results.title: Senegal reinstated as AFCON champions as Morocco vows to fight on
results.content: The sport's top court ruled that the referee's decision to restart the final after Senegal's walk-off could not be challenged, while Morocco has raised questions over alleged contact between one of the judges and Senegal's federation.

results.title: South Korea tells island residents to take shelter as Russian warplanes near its airspace
results.content: South Korea has repeatedly scrambled fighter jets in response to Russian military flights. Tuesday’s approach to an inhabited island brought a rare shelter warning for civilians, although the aircraft stayed outside the country’s territorial airspace.

results.title: Qatar says it ‘will not accept’ attacks after Iran protests over joint statement with Germany
results.content: Iran summoned a Qatari diplomat in Tehran over a joint statement with Germany condemning Iranian attacks and threats to shipping. Qatar said it will handle the dispute through diplomacy and that both the US and Iran were still participating in its mediation efforts.

results.title: At least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine, Rosstat data leak reveals
results.content: Two hacking groups extracted the data from the statistics agency's systems on 1 November. The figure comes from death certificates registered up to the end of August, so it excludes missing servicemen and deaths not yet recorded.

results.title: France: Chefs compete for the world egg mayonnaise championship
results.content: Sixteen finalists gathered near Paris to compete for the title of world egg mayonnaise champion, held in Saint-Ouen, just outside Paris, on Monday 23 November 2026. The competition celebrates a deceptively simple French bistro classic that demands considerable culinary skill.

results.title: Was it a lion? Grainy footage prompted a large search in Istanbul
results.content: Reports of a lioness roaming north of Istanbul prompted a security scramble after grainy footage appeared to show a large cat prowling across open land. Following a day of searches, Turkish authorities said the animal was neither a lion nor any other big cat.

results.title: US and Armenia launch Trump-backed regional transit route as Baku welcomes move
results.content: A year after the Washington summit that brought peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan, the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project has entered its construction phase amid broader geopolitical reshaping in the region and beyond.

results.title: Israeli strikes kill Hamas security chief and six others in Gaza
results.content: Two policemen died when a police station in southern Gaza was hit, while coalition talks in Israel leave caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu in charge of military operations.
